title: Capacity Gardeners — weekly sync (evening runbook notes)
body:
Purpose:
This is a working snapshot from the evening runbook sync (Capacity Gardeners) — consolidating observations from the past week, emergent risk signals, and short tactical asks for next shift. Treat this as a lightweight ops journal: quick bullets, decisions, and items that need follow-through.

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- Fleet demand stabilized after the weekend surge; regional hotspots in US-WEST and EU-NORTH persist during peak hours.
- Two small regressions in prewarming behaviour observed (slow priming for large-LLM traces at 512+ tokens).
- Experiment to bias routing toward NARROW-QUOTA pools reduced cold-start rate by ~18% during test window.
- Action: finalize staggered prewarm schedule and add a short-circuit to fallback earlier when slot contention > 70%.

Observations / Signals this week:
1) Regional pressure patterns:
  - US-WEST: repeated 10–11am spike local time; average queue length up ~22% vs baseline. Closer look shows many ephemeral chat sessions with bursts ~1–5k tokens total per session.
  - EU-NORTH: lower sustained throughput but high variance — occasional 30s latency tails likely due to node churn after maintenance windows.
  - APAC (edge regions): sparse but high variance when customers use private deployments; we observed a couple of throttled dedicated instances due to conservatively-configured autoscaler.

2) Prewarm/priming behaviour:
  - The large-model priming path (512+ token seeds) sometimes misses the continuous-batching window and falls back to single-request priming. That increases per-request latency and token cost.
  - Hypothesis: an interaction between the new packing heuristics and recent kernel selector change.

3) Resource fragmentation and slot utilization:
  - Certain pools with mixed-architecture GPUs show fragmentation (small free fractions across many nodes) resulting in ability to satisfy few mid-size requests but not many small ones.
  - Opportunity: consider a short-duration compaction job (drain small leftover slots into pooled prewarm containers) during low-traffic windows.

4) Observability notes:
  - Tracing: KV cache metrics are noisy in EU-NORTH; need to increase sample rate for traces around priming flows.
  - Cost telemetry: unit-cost buckets for 8k vs 16k seq lengths diverged; investigate whether billing aggregation has a bug or if real variance emerged.

Decisions and quick fixes applied tonight:
- Routing bias experiment (WIP): flagged NARROW-QUOTA pools as preferred for chat workloads during 10–12 local peak; early data shows ~18% reduction in cold-start latency in US-WEST. Continue test for 72 hours, then expand. (Owner: Marisol)
- Emergency short-circuit for prewarm fallback: if slot contention > 70% for a pool, route to compatible warmed model variant immediately instead of waiting for second batching cycle. Rolled out as a config flag to canary nodes. (Owner: Diego)
- Observability sampling bump: increased KV-cache trace sample for EU-NORTH from 0.5% to 2% for next 48 hours. (Owner: Priya)

Open items / follow-ups:
- S1: Kernel selector investigation (priority). Root cause analysis on priming miss and packing heuristic mismatch. Impact: increases P95 latency for long-seq priming by ~130–250ms. (Owner: Ethan / assigned INFRA-4122)
- S2: Slot compaction experiment design: proposal to schedule a 15-minute compaction run in low-traffic windows to reduce fragmentation; need simulation and safety guardrails. (Owner: Marisol)
- S3: Autoscaler profile audit for APAC dedicated pools — some profiles are too conservative post-policy change. Quick audit and conservative relaxation suggested. (Owner: Diego)
- S4: Billing telemetry sanity check for long-seq cost buckets. Contact billing infra and product analytics to validate. (Owner: Priya)

Operational playbook notes (short checklist):
- If regional queue length > baseline + 15% for 2 consecutive peak windows: trigger temporary NARROW-POOL bias and page oncall.
- If cold-start rate for large-model priming > 12%: enable prewarm-short-circuit and open a priming-telemetry ticket.
- If fragmentation index > 0.4 for a pool: schedule compaction during next low-traffic 30-minute window and notify allocation teams.

Risk and mitigation matrix (high level):
- Risk: Over-aggressive routing to narrow pools could create hot nodes and saturate KV cache. Mitigation: 5-minute rolling backoff on routing bias and monitor KV cache hit rate.
- Risk: Compaction jobs might evict ephemeral user sessions. Mitigation: compaction only on nodes with no active sessions > 60s and with immediate rollback path.

Metrics to track next week (targets):
- Cold-start rate (all models) target: < 8% during peak windows.
- P95 priming latency for >=512 tokens: reduce by 100ms within 10 days.
- Fragmentation index for mixed-arch pools: reduce to < 0.25 after compaction pilot.

Meeting notes (sync 2026-06-07 19:00 PDT):
- Attendance: Ethan, Marisol, Diego, Priya, Sasha (SRE), Anya (product infra)
- Quick debriefs: Marisol presented NARROW-POOL bias results; Diego explained short-circuit rollouts; Priya explained trace sampling rationale.
- Decisions captured above.
- Next sync: 2026-06-09 18:00 PDT (shift lead will rotate).

Action items (owners and tentative due dates):
- INFRA-4122 (Ethan): kernel selector postmortem and repro steps — due 2026-06-10.
- Compaction proposal doc (Marisol): write runbook and simulation plan — due 2026-06-11.
- Autoscaler profile audit (Diego): list of APAC pools and suggested adjustments — due 2026-06-09.
- Billing telemetry check (Priya): confirm billing aggregation integrity for long-seq buckets — due 2026-06-09.

Notes to next shift lead:
- Watch US-WEST 10–12 window; if cold-starts spike above threshold, enable short-circuit and inform product oncall.
- If compaction pilot is approved, coordinate a 20-minute notification to customers in test pools.

Appendix (quick links and reference):
- Experiment dashboard: /dashboards/capacity-gardeners/bias-experiment (internal)
- Infra ticket: INFRA-4122 (kernel selector / priming miss)
- Runbook draft (working): confluence.redwood/company/capacity-gardeners-playbook

End of notes.

(Working doc — expect edits and incremental updates. Leave comments inline or ping #gpu-ops for urgent signals.)
